title: Recent Robbery, Burglaries, and Peeping Incident Reported in Arlington County Crime Update - NewsBreak
text:
2 hours ago The Arlington County Police Department released its daily crime report for November 12, 2025. The report summarizes several incidents that occurred in the county in recent days. It is published every weekday except county holidays and provides initial details on major criminal events. The report is not a complete list of all police activity. All individuals mentioned are presumed innocent until proven guilty. Information may change as investigations continue.
One incident in the report was a robbery at about 7:51 p.m. on November 10 near N. Glebe Road and N. Carlin Springs Road. Two juvenile male victims were approached by six juvenile male suspects as they left a business. The suspects assaulted one victim and took his shoes. Another suspect took a jacket from the second victim. The suspects left the area on foot. Police searched the area but made no arrests. Descriptions of the suspects were provided.
Another incident involved a peeping case on the unit block of N. Bedford Street at about 8:55 p.m. on November 11. A female resident reported hearing a noise and then a male suspect speaking to her through a window. She left her home and called police. No suspect description was available. The investigation is ongoing.
The report also included a burglary on the 1200 block of S. Ross Street between 9:00 p.m. and 9:50 p.m. on November 11. The suspect or suspects entered an apartment and stole clothing and food before leaving. Police have not released any suspect descriptions.
An unlawful entry was reported on the 800 block of N. Glebe Road at about 4:19 a.m. on November 11. Two male suspects forced entry into a secured package room and stole packages and equipment. Both suspects were described, but they have not been located.
The report also mentioned a burglary on the 600 block of 24th Street S. from November 5, but details were not included. The Arlington County Police Department is investigating these incidents. Residents can check the online Crime Data Hub for more information or updates.
